twitter.lead: A feed that learns from you

linkedin.title: Most news feeds are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
It is a subtle but important difference. When an algorithm is built solely for engagement, it often prioritizes outrage or sensationalism because those topics trigger immediate reactions. But a recommendation engine can be built differently. It can be built to learn what you actually care about over time.

At Headlinne, we look at personalization as a way to respect your time. Instead of guessing what might make you click based on broad demographics, our system learns from your reading habits. If you skip a story on tech policy but dive deep into renewable energy updates, the engine adjusts. It is not about creating a filter bubble. It is about curation that evolves alongside your interests.

True personalization means you see the stories that matter to you without having to hunt for them. It is the difference between being bombarded with noise and having a digital assistant that knows your priorities.

story_card.headline: How human cells fix broken DNA
story_card.standfirst: Scientists have captured a rare look at how our bodies repair dangerous genetic damage.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers at Johns Hopkins University mapped how cells fix double-strand DNA breaks.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Two new scientific studies used advanced imaging to observe this complex repair process.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These breaks are among the most dangerous types of genetic damage for our cells.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future research will likely build on these findings to better understand cell health.

story_card.caption:
Scientists at Johns Hopkins University have discovered how human cells repair DNA double strand breaks.

This research provides a new look at a vital process that keeps our genetic code intact. Understanding these emergency repairs could lead to better insights into how our bodies protect themselves from serious damage.
